iFixit's teardown of the new AirPods 5 is out, revealing one important but very subtle repairability improvement. Watch the video below.

Repair score hits an all-time high of 2/10

Since Apple launched the original AirPods in 2016, iFixit has consistently given them a repairability score of 0/10. From heavily glued batteries and soldered connections, to a shell that's nearly impossible to open and re-assemble without damage, AirPods have always been notorious for being extremely difficult to repair.

However, iFixit says Apple has taken a small step in the right direction with the new AirPods 5 — provided the repair is done by a professional technician or a particularly adventurous DIY enthusiast.

In their latest teardown video, iFixit shows that the battery inside each earbud can be removed and replaced without destroying the AirPods — earning AirPods their first ever non-zero repairability score.

Granted, the new AirPods 5 only scored 2/10, but that's still two more points than all previous models combined.

iFixit notes that the left and right batteries aren't interchangeable, as they have reversed polarity and slightly different contact point positions.

That said, that's basically all there is to the AirPods 5's repairability. As iFixit demonstrates in the video, getting any further into the earbuds themselves without destroying them is still impossible, and the charging case is no different.

iFixit's teardown also features the always-entertaining CT scan images, giving a detailed look at how Apple has crammed the battery, MEMS microphone, H2 chip and other tiny components extremely densely inside each earbud.
